name: Step-by-Step Shower Tile Replacement: How a Professional Install Works

step.name: Step 1: Substrate demolition and framing inspection
step.text: The crew strips away old tile, damaged drywall, or failing backer boards down to the bare studs. This lets us check for hidden moisture issues, framing rot, or out-of-square corners that must be repaired before any new board goes up.

step.name: Step 2: Substrate preparation and backing board installation
step.text: Approved cementitious or waterproof backer units are hung and mechanically fastened to the framing. Seams and fastener heads are taped and treated with compatible mortar to create an entirely flat, rigid, and stable plane for tile adhesion.

step.name: Step 3: Waterproofing membrane application
step.text: A continuous waterproofing sheet or liquid-applied membrane is installed across all wet areas and tied directly into the shower pan and drain assembly. This critical barrier ensures that moisture getting behind the grout never touches your home's wooden framing.

step.name: Step 4: Layout dry run and mortar application
step.text: Tiles are measured and centered to avoid awkward, sliver-thin cuts in high-visibility corners. High-grade modified thin-set mortar is applied with a notched trowel, ensuring adequate coverage and transfer across the entire back of each tile.

step.name: Step 5: Tile setting and alignment
step.text: Tile or natural stone pieces are pressed into the mortar bed using spacers and leveling clips to prevent lippage. Cutouts for shower valves, plumbing fixtures, and recessed niches are carefully made using specialized wet saws and dust-controlled tools.

step.name: Step 6: Grouting, caulking, and curing
step.text: Once the setting mortar has fully cured according to manufacturer specs, grout is worked into the joints and cleaned. All changes of plane are sealed with flexible, mold-resistant sealant, and the shower is left to dry before regular water exposure.
